cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I saved you a front-row seat at my concert. Do you understand why it hurt?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I knew. I still looked at that empty seat before every song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed someone there who knew what this meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You'd heard me practise for months. Please tell me you understand why someone else couldn't fill it.

mechanism: A presides over which explanation of a missed concert counts and requires B to acknowledge why their particular presence mattered.
confusable: D75 names emotional cost; D99 emphasizes why B action hurt rather than merely admitting the event.
comparison: An empty seat after months of practice differs from a dinner question after job-loss news.
seedUse: Use D99-a work warning and B meaning-aware listener inference to develop why a substitute audience member was insufficient.
